title: task-pipeline execution result
description: The answer half of the family's task contract (CTX-01, beside execution-packet.schema.json). An attempt starts with an AttemptGrant — a structured object from the single authority, carrying the graph revision it was issued at and the fence that supersedes it; a bare boolean is NOT a grant, because `true` cannot say who granted what, against which revision, or whether it has since been superseded. The attempt answers with this envelope: the candidate change (content-addressed), every check actually run with its honest status (NOT_RUN is never PASS), and the evidence rows in the fact/defect/unknown-effect union. A candidate built against an older revision than the current one is STALE and cannot validate as current — it goes back through re-planning, never quietly forward. `scripts/packet.py validate-result` is the dependency-free runtime half.

schema_version.description: Contract version. An unknown major is rejected, never skimmed — same rule as the packet.

built_against_revision.description: The graph revision the candidate was built against. Compared to the CURRENT revision at validation: older means stale, and stale means re-plan.

commit.description: The candidate commit, where one exists.

changed.description: Every path the candidate changed, content-addressed — the receipt a reviewer can verify against the tree.

checks.description: Every check actually run — and the ones that could not run, as NOT_RUN with what it would take. An empty list is a result nobody verified, which the consumer may refuse.

evidence.description: Observations in the union evidence-docs and project-audit share: a FACT (observed, with its receipt), a DEFECT (observed wrong), or an UNKNOWN_EFFECT (could not be established) — three different verdicts that never blend.

status.description: The attempt's own verdict about itself. `completed` with failing checks is a contradiction the validator refuses.

name.description: What the output IS to a consumer. Never a credential — a name that reads as one (token, secret, password, api_key, credential, cookie, private_key) is refused by the validator: a result outlives its session exactly like the packet (FIX-PF-05.03).

outputs.description: TYPED outputs the attempt produced, content-addressed. A consumer binds to a named output's digest — which is what makes a changed predecessor output DETECTABLE downstream (see `consumed`).

packet_digest.description: sha256 of the immutable dispatch packet this attempt ran from (FIX-PF-05.01). Ties the answer to the exact question; a result naming a packet digest the coordinator does not recognise is a result about different work.

consumed.description: The predecessor outputs this attempt READ, by name + digest. Freshness is a comparison, not a feeling: when a predecessor re-runs and its output digest changes, every result that consumed the old digest is STALE and the node rebuilds at a new revision.

attemptGrant.description: What the single authority issued. A boolean confirmation is not a grant: it names no issuer, no revision, no fence — nothing a later reader could check.

fence.description: Monotonic token from the authority. A newer fence supersedes this grant: a result carrying an old fence lost its exclusivity mid-flight and must not land as current.

status.description: NOT_RUN and ERROR are their own statuses — never upgraded to PASS, never folded into FAIL.
